library(symcompR)
x <- Symbol("x")

This vignette covers `sympy.polys.numberfields`, including Galois groups of
polynomials, algebraic numbers, minimal polynomials, and rings of integers.

## Galois groups

`galois_group()` computes the Galois group of an irreducible polynomial over
the rationals, up to degree six. With `by_name = TRUE` it returns the name of
the transitive group, and a flag that is `TRUE` when the group is contained
in the alternating group.

```{r}
galois_group(x^4 - 2, by_name = TRUE)
galois_group(x^3 - 3 * x + 1, by_name = TRUE)
galois_group(x^5 - x + 1, by_name = TRUE)
group_order(galois_group(x^3 + 2)[[1]])
```

$x^4 - 2$ has the dihedral group of order 8, $x^3 - 3x + 1$ is cyclic, and
$x^5 - x + 1$ has the full symmetric group, so its roots cannot be written
with radicals.

### The transitive groups

The Galois group is identified among the transitive subgroups of $S_n$.
`S1TransitiveSubgroups` through `S6TransitiveSubgroups` list their names,
and `get_perm_group()` returns a concrete permutation group for a name.

```{r}
S4TransitiveSubgroups
S5TransitiveSubgroups
length(S6TransitiveSubgroups)
S1TransitiveSubgroups$S1
S2TransitiveSubgroups$S2
S3TransitiveSubgroups$A3
group_order(get_perm_group(S4TransitiveSubgroups$D4))
is_cyclic(get_perm_group(S4TransitiveSubgroups$V))
four_group()
```

The groups used for degree five and six have their own constructors:

```{r}
M20()
vapply(list(M20(), PSL2F5(), PGL2F5(), S3_in_S6(), A4_in_S6(), S4m(),
            S4p(), A4xC2(), S4xC2(), G18(), G36m(), G36p(), G72()),
       group_order, 0)
```

`tschirnhausen_transformation()` replaces a polynomial by another one with
the same splitting field, which the algorithm uses when a resolvent has
repeated roots.

```{r}
tschirnhausen_transformation(Poly(x^2 + x + 1, x))
```

## Algebraic numbers

`minimal_polynomial()` finds the minimal polynomial of an algebraic number,
and `primitive_element()` finds a single generator for a field extension such
as $\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt2, \sqrt3) = \mathbb{Q}(\sqrt2 + \sqrt3)$.

```{r}
minimal_polynomial(sqrt(S(2)) + sqrt(S(3)), x)
minimal_polynomial(S(2)^Rational(1, 3) + 1, x)
minimal_polynomial(cos(sym_pi / 7), x)
primitive_element(list(sqrt(S(2)), sqrt(S(3))), x)
```

`field_isomorphism()` expresses one generator in terms of another: below,
$\sqrt2 = \tfrac12\theta^3 - \tfrac92\theta$ for $\theta = \sqrt2 + \sqrt3$.

```{r}
field_isomorphism(sqrt(S(2)), sqrt(S(2)) + sqrt(S(3)))
to_number_field(sqrt(S(2)), sqrt(S(2)) + sqrt(S(3)))
```

`AlgebraicNumber()` represents an element of a number field by its
coordinates in a power basis.

```{r}
an <- AlgebraicNumber(sqrt(S(2)), c(1, 1))
an
minimal_polynomial(an, x)
```

### Rings of integers and prime decomposition

`round_two()` computes an integral basis of the ring of integers of a number
field, together with the field discriminant. `prime_decomp()` factors a
rational prime into prime ideals.

```{r}
round_two(x^3 + x^2 - 2 * x + 8)
prime_decomp(2, x^3 + x^2 - 2 * x + 8)
```

The field defined by $x^3 + x^2 - 2x + 8$ is a classic example of Dedekind:
the prime 2 splits into three distinct prime ideals, but this cannot be seen
from the factorization of the polynomial modulo 2, because 2 divides the
index of $\mathbb{Z}[\theta]$ in the ring of integers.

### Working with field elements

An `AlgebraicNumber` is an element $\sum c_i \theta^i$ of the field
$\mathbb{Q}(\theta)$. `field_element()` makes another element of the same
field, `to_root()` gives the number as an expression, and
`minpoly_of_element()` its minimal polynomial. `isolate()` finds a rational
isolating interval for a real algebraic number.

```{r}
b <- AlgebraicNumber(sqrt(S(2)), c(1, 1))
field_element(b, c(1, 2))
to_root(b)
minpoly_of_element(b, x)
is_primitive_element(b)
to_primitive_element(b)
isolate(sqrt(S(2)))
```

`extract_fundamental_discriminant()` writes a discriminant as a fundamental
discriminant times a square. `prime_decomp()` splits a rational prime into
prime ideals, and `prime_valuation()` gives the valuation of an ideal at a
prime ideal; the whole ring of integers has valuation 0.

```{r}
extract_fundamental_discriminant(-432)
T <- Poly(x^3 + x^2 - 2 * x + 8, x)
P <- prime_decomp(2, T)
prime_valuation(P[[1]]$ZK, P[[1]])
```
